narrative.overview:
The page is a metro operations control room at night, built from the app's own colours. Every project is a line, every agent a train, and the stations are the five jobs: Plan, Steer, Monitor, Review, with Edit as a spur that loops back off Review. The hero is a live line diagram; the five feature rows hang off one continuous blue track rail; product screens sit on the wall as monitors.

The ground is the app's navy, deepened for the page. Blue is the one action colour. The four line colours (emerald, amber, rose, violet) mark lines and states, and the focused station is the brightest thing on screen while the rest dims. Density is calm: one 12-column grid, generous section padding, hairline dividers instead of fills.

Depth is quiet: flat navy surfaces separated by 1px hairlines, with long soft black shadows under monitors and panels only.
keyCharacteristics: Navy ground taken from the app screenshots, with panel, raised and hairline steps of the same hue.
Straight track with 45-degree turns only; no arcs anywhere in a diagram.
Stations are white ticks with a dark keyline; station name plates are white on action blue.
State is a mark as well as a hue: hollow ring (needs input), half ring (working), filled dot (done).
Overpass display, Archivo body, JetBrains Mono only for commands, paths and project names.

rules.name: The Line Colours Are Lines Rule
rules.body: Emerald, amber, rose and violet colour a line, a train or a state mark, never a panel, a heading or a button. One carve-out: violet is also the Pro mark (the Pro badge pill, the workflow loop-back track and the Workflow list ticks).

rules.name: The One Action Blue Rule
rules.body: Every filled control is action blue with white text; no second button colour exists.

rules.name: The Focus Is Brightest Rule
rules.body: In a diagram the focused station or node is full white and full opacity; every other station sits at 60% or in muted.

rules.name: The Mono Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only for literal strings a user would type or read off a tool: commands, URLs, paths, build names, project names.

rules.name: The Tape Names An Object Rule
rules.body: Label tape names a thing on screen (a nav target, a column, a monitor). It never sits above a heading as a section label.

rules.name: The One Loud Line Rule
rules.body: Rank comes from size alone: one H1 at display scale, everything else visibly smaller.

rules.name: The One Track Rule
rules.body: The feature rows share one rail with no gap between rows; each row adds a station tick on it, never a separate card.

rules.name: The Soft Black Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, black and fall downward. No glow, no coloured shadow, no hard offset.

dos: Do draw every track straight with 45-degree turns; stations are white ticks with a dark keyline.
Do put every product screen and illustration in a monitor frame (8px, hairline, monitor well).
Do mark state with shape and hue together, next to a text label.
Do label every HTML/SVG illustration "Illustration" in its title bar.
Do keep a static equivalent for every motion under reduced motion, and a pause control for the looping diagram.
Do keep tap targets at 44px minimum (48px for buttons).
donts: Don't draw arcs or curves in a track or graph.
Don't fill panels, headings or buttons with emerald, amber, rose or violet; the violet Pro badge is the only filled line-colour shape.
Don't set prose in mono or headings in anything but Overpass.
Don't put label tape above a heading as an eyebrow.
Don't add glow, coloured shadows or hard offset shadows.
